extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, scientists, and thinkers seeking a method for acquiring reliable knowledge (early-modern/experimental philosophers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for discovering and validating natural-philosophical knowledge by identifying and removing mental idols, ordering experiment and induction correctly, and preferring fruitful, well-defined inquiry over sectarian dogma or narrow empiricism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance observing differences and resemblances
rubrics_metrics.description: Some minds are vigorous at observing differences, others at observing resemblances; both tendencies can fall into excess.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interchange and employ both modes in turn so the understanding is 'at once penetrating and capacious' — avoid catching at 'nice distinctions' or 'shadows of resemblance'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid partisan reverence for antiquity or novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Some evince unbounded admiration of antiquity, others embrace novelty; few preserve the just medium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Truth is not to be sought in the fortune of a conjuncture of time; abjure factions of ancients vs moderns and judge by nature and experience, not by age or novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate particular and general contemplation
rubrics_metrics.description: Contemplation of individual forms distracts, while contemplation of general composition stupefies the understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interchange attention to particulars and to general structures so the mind neither neglects details nor becomes bewildered by abstractions; the two species of contemplation must be employed in turn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspect what particularly fixes your understanding (idols of the den)
rubrics_metrics.description: Idols of the den arise from a predominant pursuit, excess in synthesis/analysis, party zeal for certain ages, or the extent/narrowness of the subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: He who contemplates nature should suspect whatever particularly takes and fixes his understanding and take special caution to preserve equable and unprejudiced judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be wary of the idols of the market (words and names)
rubrics_metrics.description: Words and names entwine themselves round the understanding; men imagine reason governs words while words react upon the understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceed advisedly, bring disputes to regular issue by definitions, but recognize definitions themselves are words — therefore rely on particular instances and their regular series and arrangement to determine notions and axioms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid fanciful or confused names (idols of words)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two kinds: names of things with no existence (fictitious abstractions) and names of actual objects that are confusedly or irregularly abstracted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exterminate fictitious names by refutation or desuetude of theories; remedy confused abstractions by examining the multiplicity of significations (example: 'moist' has many inconsistent senses) and by careful verification before predication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer concrete substance-terms over abstract quality-terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Names of substances (less abstract, more defined species) are less faulty; words denoting actions are more faulty; words denoting qualities (except immediate objects of sense) are most faulty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When possible, use clearer, less abstract terms and verify notions by sensory instances; expect degrees of distortion and treat quality-terms with special skepticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject the idols of the theatre (theoretical dogmas)
rubrics_metrics.description: Idols of the theatre are instilled by the fictions of theories and depraved rules of demonstration; entire sects/theories may mislead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid attempting exhaustive confutations of all sects; instead, adopt a method that levels individual acuteness (use tools and procedure) so demonstrations do not enslave the mind; prefer methods that make discovery less dependent on individual wit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid the three corrupting sources of false philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: False philosophies arise from three sources: the sophistic (overly logical/theoretical), the empiric (confined to few experiments), and the superstitious (mixing theology/fancy with philosophy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize examples (Aristotle as sophistic; alchemists and Gilbert as empiric dangers; Pythagoras/Plato as examples of superstition) and guard against each: do not let logic outrun experience, do not generalize from too few experiments, and avoid theological conflation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep natural philosophy distinct from theology and superstition
rubrics_metrics.description: Corrupting philosophy by mixing it with superstition/theology is injurious; some moderns have tried to build natural philosophy on Scripture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use greatest caution — render unto faith the things that are faith's — avoid deriving natural-philosophical systems from sacred texts or theological doctrines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on secondary qualities and active operations rather than unfounded primary forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Physicians and natural philosophers should examine secondary qualities (attraction, repulsion, attenuation, inspissation, dilatation, astringency, separation, maturation) rather than speculate on elements, occult properties, or primary forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate the actual operations and processes of bodies and advance to third and fourth qualities instead of reducing phenomena prematurely to first qualities or hypothetical primary forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize active/operative principles over stationary principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Contemplation of stationary principles (what things are from) is less useful than investigation of active principles (how things are created and operate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value observations that lead to practice; avoid overvaluing divisions like generation, corruption, augmentation, diminution, alteration, translation as mere popular measures rather than explanations of causes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid abstract extremes (atoms/potential matter) disconnected from utility
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstraction to potential and shapeless matter or down to atoms often yields little value for advancing human estate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concentrate on intermediate objects and useful causes rather than endless dissection toward ultimate minutiae divorced from practical import.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard against intemperance: dogmatism and scepticism
rubrics_metrics.description: Excesses: hasty decision making that makes sciences positive and dictatorial; or radical skepticism that enervates inquiry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a balanced temperament: avoid arbitrary dogma (which subdues inquiry) and avoid paralysing scepticism (which prevents rigorous investigation); supply assistance to senses and understanding without despairing of discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct the fourfold fallacies in demonstration from senses to axioms
rubrics_metrics.description: The process from senses to axioms errs four ways: (1) impressions of the senses are erroneous; (2) notions are improperly abstracted and confused; (3) induction is improper, relying on simple enumeration without exclusions/resolutions; (4) the common method of beginning with most general propositions then deducing intermediates is the parent of error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply and correct sensory defects, refine abstractions, employ proper induction (including exclusions and resolutions), and avoid top-down proof-methods — instead lay down a true way of interpreting nature via corrected induction and experimental method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use experience as demonstration only when tightly tied to the actual experiment
rubrics_metrics.description: Experience is the best demonstration provided it adhere to the experiment actually made; transferring experimental results carelessly becomes fallacious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design experiments methodically, extend inquiry beyond solitary matters, and be cautious when generalizing from one experiment to other subjects; avoid 'blind and stupid' experimentation and chance wandering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design experiments to elicit causes and axioms (light) rather than immediate profit
rubrics_metrics.description: In true course of experiment we should seek experiments which afford light — discovery of causes and axioms — rather than immediate practical gain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize experiments that generate general axioms which yield many effects and broaden practice; avoid premature rush to application for fame or profit without securing causes or axioms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge philosophies by their fruits (productivity and useful effects)
rubrics_metrics.description: Of all signs none is more certain than that of the fruits produced — systems should be judged by their works; futile systems are unproductive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value practical discoveries and improvements (mechanical arts, technical progress) as signs of sound philosophy; treat doctrines that yield only dispute and contention as suspect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer systems that grow and improve (sign of being founded on nature)
rubrics_metrics.description: Theories founded on nature grow and increase; those founded on opinion stagnate and fail to improve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the progress and increase of specific sciences as a sign: mechanical arts that improve show a natural foundation, whereas philosophies that remain stationary indicate a defect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat the confessions and limits admitted by authorities as diagnostic
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorities who confess the subtilty of nature or the weakness of human wit often use that to deny possibility of discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be skeptical of appeals to impossibility by established authors; such confessions can indicate the limits of their method, not limits of nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider dissension and unanimity as signs of methodological soundness
rubrics_metrics.description: Great dissension among philosophers indicates the way from senses to understanding was not well prepared; apparent unanimity often stems from prejudice or authority rather than free judgement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: View persistent controversies as evidence of unsound methods; be wary of unanimity as a positive sign (it often indicates obsequiousness rather than true agreement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Level reliance on individual wit with procedural tools and steadiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Discovery should depend less on individual acuteness and more on steady method and instruments (analogy: rulers and compasses vs freehand drawing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt methods and instruments that reduce dependence on individual talent, making the process of discovery more regular and accessible.
